subject: Nan value for AIC and BIC in summary(glmmTMB)

messages.author: 98e4df62972c9c66
messages.subject: Nan value for AIC and BIC in summary(glmmTMB)
parts:
Hi

I was running a glmmTMB with generalized poisson distribution (Poisson underdispersed data), 
but summary() is incomplete.  
here is the code :

mymodel = glmmTMB(nb_class~nb_phylum+(nb_phylum|phylum_type/empo_3)+(nb_phylum|empo_3/PI)+(nb_phylum|sample),datsc,family=genpois(link = "log"))
summary(mymodel)

 Family: genpois  ( log )
Formula:          nb_class ~ nb_phylum + (nb_phylum | phylum_type/empo_3) + (nb_phylum |  
    empo_3/PI) + (nb_phylum | sample)
Data: datsc

     AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
      NA       NA       NA       NA    33696 

Random effects:

Conditional model:
 Groups             Name        Variance Std.Dev. Corr  
 sample             (Intercept) 0.014280 0.11950        
                    nb_phylum   0.001471 0.03836  -1.00 
 empo_3:phylum_type (Intercept) 0.074384 0.27273        
                    nb_phylum   0.040788 0.20196  -0.05 
 PI:empo_3          (Intercept) 0.015560 0.12474        
                    nb_phylum   0.029464 0.17165  0.37  
 phylum_type        (Intercept) 0.561571 0.74938        
                    nb_phylum   0.038275 0.19564  0.58  
 empo_3             (Intercept) 0.004829 0.06949        
                    nb_phylum   0.046730 0.21617  1.00  
Number of obs: 33714, groups:  sample, 2000; empo_3:phylum_type, 911; PI:empo_3, 117; phylum_type, 84; empo_3, 17

Overdispersion parameter for genpois family (): 0.24 

Conditional model:
            Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept) -0.03764    0.09025  -0.417    0.677    
nb_phylum    0.39492    0.06643   5.945 2.76e-09 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1


Have you any idea of how to fix that ?
Thanks
Nay

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Nan value for AIC and BIC in summary(glmmTMB)
parts:
Please ask glmmTMB questions on r-sig-mix...@r-project.org *or*
post a reproducible issue at https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/issues
(the latter sounds more appropriate).

It looks like you have a singular fit (see -1/+1 correlations for the
sample and empo_3 grouping variables), that may be the problem.

I don’t think it’s an issue. Unconverged Models in glmmTMB intentionally have their AIC reported as NA. We mentioned this in the R Journal paper.

Mollie

messages.author: 98e4df62972c9c66
messages.subject: Re: Nan value for AIC and BIC in summary(glmmTMB)
parts:
The problem was fixed by droping sample and empo_3 random effect on intercept (and keeping it only on slope)!
Thanks a lot!
Nay
